metadata.title: Crypto stocks slide premarket as Bitcoin selloff continues

content.text:
Investing.com -- Shares of crypto-related companies fell sharply in premarket trading Monday as Bitcoin (BTC-USD) slipped to about $64,600.50, staying close to its lowest level in three months.
Strategy, (MSTR) formerly known as MicroStrategy, dropped over 7%, as did BitMine and Galaxy Digital. Circle (CRCL) fell 7.6%, Coinbase (COIN) declined 6.4%, while Robinhood (HOOD) and Hut 8 lost more than 5% each.
Tracking Bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies also fell, extending steep losses over recent weeks as sentiment toward the sector has soured.
Worries about higher U.S. interest rates and an uncertain regulatory outlook have kept pressure on digital assets. Recent inflation data has strengthened bets that the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December, with some traders pricing in a 50-basis-point increase.
Higher rates typically weigh on speculative assets like crypto. Bitcoin has historically lagged during past Fed tightening cycles, notably in 2022 and 2023.
Caution ahead of Nvidia's earnings this week also kept traders on the sidelines, amid weaker risk appetite more broadly. Nvidia shares have fallen sharply in recent sessions after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing
MSCI added to the strain by saying it will remove all Treasury companies, chiefly Strategy, from its indexes at the end of November. The change limits Strategy's access to capital and raises the prospect of asset sales as the company works to meet mounting debt and capital obligations.
